newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 1.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Following Albanian President Sali Berisha's concession of defeat yesterday after Sunday's national poll, the neighbouring country is now on the difficult road to restoring peace and order. According to unofficial figures, the Socialist Party had garnered 55 percent of the vote and 73 seats in Parliament. The second round of elections will be held on Sunday.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis stressed yesterday that the vision of a large and strong Europe was not only a chase for the right economic indicators. "Our vision of Europe is wider and expresses our values, our ambitions for a better life, more freedom and social justice," he said at a function on "The Europe We Want", also attended by former European Commission President Jacques Delors.

--Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos nudged Britain's Arts Minister Mark Fisher on a return of the Parthenon Marbles when they met in Luxembourg yesterday, but Fisher reiterated that Britain would not return the 5th century BC artworks.
--Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides is in Athens today for talks on the stance Cyprus will take in talks scheduled for July 9-13 in New York under UN auspices.

--The president of Greece's most successful telecoms firm Intracom Socrates Kokkalis went on the offensive against Development Minister Vasso Papandreou yesterday, criticising her calls for a 10 percent corporate tax to fund programmes for the unemployed.
--There's feverish activity at the tax department to recoup the 1.65 trillion drachmas owed to the state. A new list of names of debtors owing more than five million drachmas each is being prepared.
--A third autopsy on the body of a young recruit found dead on an Evros army base last week has reportedly found no indications of foul play.

--Sean Connery and upcoming starlet Lolita Davidovic will star in a forthcoming movie on the life of Andreas Papandreou, the late founder of socialist PASOK, and his third and last wife Dimitra Liani, according to reports.

--The government will place its proposals on combatting unemployment on the table today in scheduled talks with employers and unions. Among the proposals are the introduction of a 35-hour working week without a reduction in pay. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
